name: Copper engraving
region: The Upper Rhine, Nuremberg, Antwerp and Haarlem
summary: A picture cut into a copper plate with a burin, inked into the grooves and printed under great pressure. Schongauer and Dürer made it an art; Goltzius made the swelling line a show of skill; for three centuries it reproduced paintings and maps.

philosophy.core_thesis: A burin line that swells and tapers in polished copper gives the finest and most even tone that a hand can make.
design_principles: Build every tone from lines that swell in the middle and taper at both ends.
Lay the lines in systems: parallel lines for a half tone, a second set crossed at 30–45° for the shadow, and dots in the gaps (dot-and-lozenge) for the deepest dark.
Turn each line round the form, like the lines of a contour map, so the swell shows the light.
Keep the line pitch at 80–150 a inch; the eye at reading distance sees a grey, not lines.
Leave a clear plate mark 10–20 mm outside the image, with the title and the names of the designer and the engraver in the margin.
Print in one black or dark brown ink on dampened paper.
anti_patterns: Hatching that does not follow the form
A soft, grained tone with no lines
A coloured fill or a flat area of solid ink
Trimmed margins that cut off the plate mark

process.matrix: A polished copper plate, 1–2 mm thick, cut with a lozenge-section burin pushed by the palm.
process.press: A roller press with felt blankets that pushes the dampened paper into the grooves.
process.image_making: The engraver transfers the drawing, cuts the lines, removes the burr with a scraper, and proofs the plate in states.
process.edition: Some hundreds of good impressions before the lines wear; later plates were steel-faced for thousands.

inks.strategy: One stiff black or brown-black ink, rubbed into the lines and wiped from the surface.

screening.rule: Make the tone with swelling burin lines at 80–150 a inch, crossed in the shadows.

registration.rule: One plate prints all the image; there is no register.

substrate.stock: Laid rag paper made by hand, dampened before the print.
substrate.finish: Laid or later wove, soft and with little sizing so that it takes the ink from the lines.

surface.impression: A deep plate mark round the image and a sharp relief of each line, which a finger can feel.
surface.sheen: The ink stands up from the paper with a slight gloss.
surface.texture: A silver-grey of fine lines; under a lens each line has a pointed start and end.

emotion.target_response: Precision and authority: the viewer trusts a picture of skilled, patient work.

avoid_when: The image needs colour or a soft, loose line.
The brand wants to look casual or playful.

modifiers.how: Draw the lines in a wax ground with a needle and bite them in acid; the line is even and free, not swelled.
Rock the plate to a grain and scrape the lights, so the tone has no lines.

sources.title: Antony Griffiths, Prints and Printmaking (British Museum Press, 1996)
